entities.summary: Hans von Aachen was a German painter who was one of the leading representatives of Northern Mannerism. Born in Nuremberg, Germany around 1550, von Aachen trained under the renowned artist Lucas Cranach the Elder. His innovative style, characterized by intricate details and use of chiaroscuro, influenced a generation of artists, including Peter Paul Rubens and Rembrandt van Rijn. Von Aachen's work can be found in prominent museums such as the Alte Pinakothek in Munich and the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna. His legacy continues to inspire artists and art historians today. The artist's exact birthdate remains unknown, but his death in 1615 marked the end of an era in German art. Von Aachen's contributions to the development of Northern Mannerism have had a lasting impact on the art world.
